topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and set out the lecture's learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional modalities and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional approaches to cancer management, focusing on local interventions and the mechanisms, toxicities, and efflux-mediated resistance of cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific biological vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological defects in cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependencies, checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the targeting of hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the various molecular mechanisms through which tumor cells develop drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and mechanisms of action of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor cell-surface markers.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for tumor immunosurveillance and evaluate strategies to activate or engineer T cells to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Challenges, mortality trends, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching evaluation of modern cancer therapy, discussing systemic challenges, historical changes in mortality, and future therapeutic paradigms.
